title: Manage ReadStat patches as git diffs
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

`update_readstat()` now tracks the ReadStat `dev` branch (since releases are slow) and automatically applies the small set of patches in `patches/readstat/`. Each patch is a git diff whose header links to the upstream ReadStat PR and the haven issue it fixes, so it's easy to drop once merged upstream. `apply_iconv_hack()` is converted into a patch as well, and WizardMac/ReadStat#355 is backported (adapted to dev, where it no longer applies cleanly).

Fixes #724.

title: Store metadata in a single S7 `haven_meta` attribute
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Work in progress towards #710, #712, #718, #719, and #799: replaces haven's scattered metadata attributes (`format.*`, `display_width`, `width`, `notes`, `*_timestamp`) with a single `haven_meta` attribute holding an S7 object. See `plan.md` for the design.

Done so far:

* S7 classes (`meta_var_sas`/`_spss`/`_stata`, `meta_df_sas`/`_spss`/`_stata`), `meta()`/`meta<-`, and fallback to legacy attributes.
* `zap_meta()`; `zap_formats()` and `zap_widths()` deprecated.
* Readers populate `haven_meta` (and no longer set legacy attributes), capturing new fields: SAS informat/width/table name/xpt version, SPSS width/measure/alignment/MR sets, Stata storage type/version. S7 objects are built in C++ from prototypes, because validated construction costs ~100µs per object (~80µs with dev S7). Reading a 10,000 column file takes 44ms vs 28ms in haven 2.5.5.
* Writers honour all metadata that ReadStat can write, so `read_*() |> write_*()` round-trips. `write_xpt()` and `write_dta()` take `version`/`name` defaults from metadata; `write_sav()` gains `label`. Stata storage types fall back to the default if the values no longer fit.

Remaining work:

- [x] vctrs: carry `haven_meta` through `vec_ptype2()`/`vec_cast()` for `haven_labelled` and `haven_labelled_spss`.
- [x] Roxygen docs for `?meta`, `?meta_sas`, `?meta_spss`, `?meta_stata` (with per-file-type support tables); add them to the Metadata section of `_pkgdown.yml`.
- [x] Update `read_*()`/`write_*()` docs to link to the metadata topics.
- [x] NEWS bullets.
- [x] `devtools::check()` (currently warns about undocumented exports).
- [ ] Revdep check and coordinate with xportr/metatools.
- [x] Find test files for SPSS MR sets and `.por` metadata (both currently untested).
- [x] Decide: should Stata `version` cover files older than format 113 (currently `NULL`)? Should `meta<-` strip stale legacy attributes? Should readers have an option to skip metadata?
- [x] Remove `plan.md` before merging.

Fixes #782: `read_xpt()` now returns the namestr format width in `meta()@width`, so width round-trips through `write_xpt()`. The trailing-period half of the issue is fixed upstream in WizardMac/ReadStat#415 and will land with the next vendored ReadStat update.

title: Don't classify user-defined SAS formats as dates by prefix
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

The prefix matching added in #790 classified any SAS format starting with a short date format name as a date, so a column with the user-defined format `DAYSV` was read as `Date` instead of `numeric` (revdep failure in libr, #859).

Short date format names (`DAY`, `WEEK*`, `MON*`, `QTR`, `YEAR`) now only match when followed by a width digit, a decimal point, or nothing (`DAY2.` matches, `DAYSV` doesn't). Longer unambiguous prefixes like `MMDDYY` keep loose matching so separator variants like `MMDDYYS10.` keep working.

Verified against libr's test suite, which now passes.

title: Add progress bar to `read_*()` functions
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Fixes #730.

`read_*()` gain `progress = NULL`, which defaults to showing a cli progress bar in interactive sessions (disable with `options(haven.show_progress = FALSE)`). Progress is reported in bytes read via ReadStat's update/progress callbacks, so it works for XPT files that don't store a row count. The user interrupt check moved from the value handler into the progress callback (every 0.1% of the file).

`DfReaderInputStream` now tracks its own position because calling `tellg()` per row made XPT reads ~3x slower; timings are now unchanged from main.

Not tested: cleanup of a visible bar after Ctrl+C mid-read.

title: Reduce memory usage of reads with small `n_max`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Fixes #845.

Header-only parse of an 80 MB XPT file drops from ~39 MB to ~5 KB allocated.

title: Correct SAS dates on or after year 4000
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

SAS doesn't treat 4000 and 8000 as leap years ([SAS blog](https://blogs.sas.com/content/sasdummy/2024/02/15/calculate-leap-year-in-sas/)), so placeholder dates like 07/07/7777 and 09/09/9999 came back one and two days early. The fixture stores the raw day counts from the file in the issue.

Fixes #728.

title: Un-deprecate `write_sas()` and remove `read_sas(cols_only)`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

ReadStat now computes the sas7bdat header checksum correctly (WizardMac/ReadStat#398, already vendored), so files written by `write_sas()` are readable by SAS. `cols_only` has been deprecated since haven 2.2.0.

Closes #783

title: Reorganise and simplify `src/`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Internal refactoring of the C++ code in `src/` with no intended user-facing changes. Each commit is self-contained and should be easiest to review one at a time.

One pre-existing quirk is left alone: logical columns are written to SPSS with the "scale" measure rather than "nominal", because `measureType()` only ever sees the coerced integer vector.

🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Fixes #724.

Two upstream behavior changes required test updates:
* The XPT writer now rejects duplicate variable names, so the duplicate-names `col_select` test (covered elsewhere) was removed.
* The SAV writer now sets the string format width to match the stored width, so a roundtrip can change `format.spss` (e.g. `A100` becomes `A4`).

title: Use data file encoding for SAS catalogs without one
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

SAS catalogs usually leave the header encoding byte as 0, which ReadStat maps to WINDOWS-1252, so UTF-8 catalogs either fail to parse or produce garbled labels. The catalog from #836 turns out to be UTF-8 (the suggested `catalog_encoding = "latin1"` workaround produces mojibake).

The test fixture is the `tagged-na` pair with the data file's encoding byte set to UTF-8 and a non-ASCII label patched into the catalog.

Fixes #836.

title: Drop readr dependency
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Fixes #834.

`datasource()` now returns a bare path or raw vector and the C++ side picks the reader from the type, so the `_file`/`_raw` entry points collapse into one per format. As a side effect, the SAS data and catalog inputs no longer have to be the same kind (e.g. raw data + catalog path).

title: `write_dta()`: use smallest numeric storage type
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Like Stata's `compress`, numeric columns are now written as `byte`, `int`, `long`, or `double`, whichever is smallest while exactly representing every value. Datetimes always stay `double`. Integers too large for `long` are now written as `double` rather than erroring.

Fixes #651.

title: `write_dta()`: allow single character variable names in older versions
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

The variable name check for `version` <= 13 required at least two characters, so e.g. `write_dta(data.frame(x = 1), path, version = 13)` errored.

title: Link to iconv when R does so (fix conda)
description: Fixes #774. Closes #830.

🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Pulls in the XPT V8 reader fix that uses the OBSV8 observation count, so trailing blank rows are no longer dropped. XPT V5 has no such field, so it's unchanged.

Fixes #754.

title: Write missing strL values as empty strings
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Stata has no missing string value, so `NA` in a strL variable is now written as `""`, matching regular str# variables.

Fixes #760.

title: Detect when iconv needs -liconv in configure
description:
Fixes #774.

Adds an autoconf-style iconv link check to `configure`: if a test program calling `iconv_open`/`iconv_close` fails to link with the build flags, it's retried with `-liconv`, which is appended to `PKG_LIBS` on success. Errors out clearly if iconv can't be found either way.

title: `write_dta()`: error informatively for labels outside Stata's range
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Stata stores value label values as 4-byte integers, and values above 2,147,483,620 are reserved for missing values (`.`, `.a`–`.z`). Previously labels beyond ±2^31 errored with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed", and labels between 2,147,483,621 and 2^31 - 1 were silently read back as missing.

Fixes #739.

title: Use consistent argument checking blocks in read/write functions
description:
🤖 Written by AI, reviewed by me 🤖

Each `read_`/`write_` function now starts with a single argument checking block that checks each argument in signature order (`col_select` and `.name_repair` are still checked later by `select_cols()`). 

Fixes #737

title: Fix lossy cast check for labelled_spss() vectors containing NA
description:
Casting a `labelled_spss()` vector that contains `NA` to a `labelled_spss()` with a different `na_range` errors:

```r
x <- labelled_spss(c(1, NA, 997), na_range = c(990, 999))
y <- labelled_spss(2, na_range = c(995, 999))
vctrs::vec_cast(x, y)
#> Error in if (!any(lossy)) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

The range comparison in `vec_cast.haven_labelled_spss.haven_labelled_spss()` is `NA` for an `NA` input, which makes `lossy` `NA`, and `maybe_lossy_cast()` then fails on `if (!any(lossy))`. This is what breaks `rbind()` on data frames (and `bind_rows()` when labels also conflict) with such columns. A true `NA` is not a value switching from missing to non-missing, so it is now excluded from the range check.

I couldn't use the OECD files from the report, so the examples above are synthetic. They hit the same error message and code path.

I compared 32 casts and combinations (ranges, values, integer, character, tagged `NA`, with and without `NA`) before and after. Only the three that errored changed; everything else, including the lossy cast errors, behaves the same. The new test goes through `vec_cast()`, `vec_c()` and `rbind()`, and fails without the change. The full suite passes.

Closes #761

title: fix: warn when strl_threshold is out-of-range instead of silent clipping
description:
## Summary

`validate_strl_threshold()` previously silently clipped out-of-range values (< 0 or > 2045) to 2045 without informing the user. This PR adds a `cli_warn()` so users know their value was adjusted.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `R/haven-stata.R` | Add `cli_warn()` in `validate_strl_threshold()` when clipping occurs |
| `tests/testthat/test-haven-stata.R` | Add test for out-of-range warning; update existing test to `expect_warning()` |

## Motivation

If a user passes `strl_threshold = 5000`, they expect strings > 5000 bytes to use strL storage. But the value was silently clipped to 2045 (the max str# length). Now the user gets a warning:

```
Warning: `strl_threshold` must be between 0 and 2045, not 5000.
```

## Validation

- `devtools::test(filter = "haven-stata")`: 70 PASS, 0 new failures
- `devtools::test()`: 474 PASS, 2 pre-existing failures (labelled-pillar snapshot, haven-sas deprecation)

## Notes

- Complementary to PR #820 (strl_threshold roundtrip test) — different scope, no file overlap
- The warning uses the existing `call = caller_env()` pattern for proper error attribution

title: Clarify labelled vectors in read docs
description:
Fixes #741.

This updates the `read_*()` documentation to make the imported labelled-vector workflow more explicit for users coming from Stata, SPSS, or SAS:

- notes that value labels are preserved as `labelled()` / `labelled_spss()` intermediate representations, not regular R factors

title: Forward na.rm in median() for labelled vectors
description:
`median.haven_labelled()` in R/labelled.R takes `na.rm` but passes a hardcoded `na.rm = TRUE` to `median()`, so the user's value never reaches the computation:

```r
x <- labelled(c(1L, NA, 3L))
median(x, na.rm = FALSE)
#> [1] 2
```

The default stays `na.rm = TRUE`, so calls that rely on it behave as before. `median(x, na.rm = FALSE)` now returns `NA` and `median(x, na.rm = TRUE)` still returns `2`.

Found during my most recent [ry](https://github.com/sims1253/ry) audit.

fix: guard against zero-length label/format attributes in write functions (#740)
description:
Fixes #740

## Problem
When a variable has `label = character(0)` (zero-length character vector), `STRING_ELT(x, 0)` returns `NULL`, causing `Rf_translateCharUTF8` to crash with an error about CHARSXP.

This affects `write_dta()`, `write_sav()`, and `write_xpt()`.

## Fix
Added `Rf_length()` checks in three functions in `DfWriter.cpp`:
- `var_label()` - treats zero-length label as no label (returns NULL)
- `var_format()` - treats zero-length format as no format (falls through to default)
- `setFileLabel()` - treats zero-length file label as no label (skips)

## Changes
- `src/DfWriter.cpp`: 3 guard clauses added (1-line change each)
- `tests/testthat/test-haven-stata.R`: new test covering zero-length variable label and format attributes

## Testing
- Reprex from issue #740 now works without error
- All 64 Stata tests pass (0 failures)
- Full test suite: 439 PASS, 1 pre-existing FAILURE (SAS deprecation test unrelated to this change)

title: docs: document retained metadata for read_xpt/write_xpt (#719)
description:

- **Round-trip example**: Adds a runnable example showing that `label` and `format.sas` survive a `write_xpt()` → `read_xpt()` cycle.
- **Notes**: Documents the `notes` attribute for completeness.

This is a documentation-only change to `R/haven-sas.R`, `man/read_xpt.Rd`, and `NEWS.md`. Complements the existing `read_sas`/`read_dta`/`read_spss` metadata docs.

**Relation to #800**: PR #800 documents the `labelled()` class and value label workflow for `read_sas`/`read_dta`/`read_spss`. This PR focuses on the XPT-specific metadata that #800 does not cover. No overlap.

title: test: add strl_threshold coverage for write_dta(); fix test typo
description:

This new test verifies the threshold behavior with both a low threshold (50 bytes, forcing both strings to strL) and a high threshold (5000 bytes, keeping both as str#).

description:
This PR fixes #596, adding write support for SPSS user missing values for integers as well as doubles.

This includes a minor change to the readstat SAV writing code - this change has been made upstream and will come through in the next readstat release (see WizardMac/ReadStat#251).

One thing to note is that we need to allow for either integer or real values in the na_range attribute if the main vector is either type, since we can't cast na_range to the vector type in labelled_spss().
Although na_values are cast to the type of the vector in labelled_spss(), na_range has to allow numeric vectors so that Inf/-Inf can be represented (the equivalent of SPSS HI and LO placeholders).

title: Update labelled.R with search functions
description:
Dear package maintainers,

As suggested in #243, #443 and #444, this PR adds search functions to let the user print and find value and variable labels as easily as possible.

Target audience: typically, survey data users faced with a labelled dataset imported from SPSS or Stata, with 100s of uninformatively named variables as in `v1, v2, … v100` or `Q3a`, `q77` etc. Try importing virtually any survey from an official statistical agency to get an example.

## Example usage

Using a labelled dataset from the [`questionr`](https://github.com/juba/questionr) package:

```r
# library(haven)
> data("fertility", package = "questionr")
> ex <- women
```
Let's start with __variable labels__:
```r
print_variable_labels(ex)
```
```
Variable labels: 
# A tibble: 17 x 2
   variable          label                             
   <chr>             <chr>                             
 1 id_woman          Woman Id                          
 2 id_household      Household Id                      
 3 weight            Sample weight                     
 4 interview_date    Interview date                    
 5 date_of_birth     Date of birth                     
 6 age               Age at last anniversary (in years)
 7 residency         Urban / rural residency           
 8 region            Region                            
 9 instruction       Level of instruction              
10 employed          Employed?                         
11 matri             Matrimonial status                
12 religion          Religion                          
13 newspaper         Read newspaper?                   
14 radio             Listen to radio?                  
15 tv                Watch TV?                         
16 ideal_nb_children Ideal number of children          
17 test              Ever tested for HIV?              
```
Let's grep a few variable labels (the function currently only greps those, not names):

```r
find_variable_labels(women, "wom.n|child|hiv")
```
```
# A tibble: 3 x 2
  variable          label                   
  <chr>             <chr>                   
1 id_woman          Woman Id                
2 ideal_nb_children Ideal number of children
3 test              Ever tested for HIV?    
```
If nothing's found:
```r
find_variable_labels(women, "xyz")
```
```
# A tibble: 0 x 2
# … with 2 variables: variable <chr>, label <chr>
```
Onto __value labels__:
```r
print_labels(ex$instruction)
```
```
Labels: 
# A tibble: 4 x 2
  value label    
  <chr> <chr>    
1 0     none     
2 1     primary  
3 2     secondary
4 3     higher   
```
Silly grep example:
```r
find_labels(women$instruction, "RY")
```
```
# A tibble: 2 x 2
  value label    
  <chr> <chr>    
1 1     primary  
2 2     secondary
```
If nothing's found:
```r
find_labels(women$instruction, "xyz")
```
```
# A tibble: 0 x 2
# … with 2 variables: value <chr>, label <chr>
```

The examples in the PR use either made-up examples or use the `iris.dta` dataset provided with `haven`, but those are less illustrative than the example above, which comes closer to a real use-case.

## Breaking changes

`print_labels` invisibly returns the variable labels instead of the actual variable, as `haven` currently does. I understand this will break continuous integration, so can revert to current behaviour if needed.

## Improvements for review

- I can write tests if need be.
- I can try to use `tidyselect` as suggested in #444, although it is not yet a dependency of `haven`.
- Anything you like :)

Best wishes,

François

title: Rewrite haven_labelled with vctrs
description:
@hadley I mentioned I while ago that I could look into this: haven_labelled as a vctr. I've had a couple of false starts, but now I think I've finally managed something workable. It's still work-in-progress, but I was hoping you could have a quick look to see if I'm on the right track. I have this nagging feeling that I'm missing something, and this should be simpler; especially my ptype2 methods feel "hacky".

Key points about the type system:
- Refuse to combine two labelled vectors if they have different sets of labels.
- Otherwise, coercion follows same rules as underlying data types.
- Combining a bare type with a labelled type results in a labelled type.
- Casts from one labelled to another are lossy if previously labelled data would become unlabelled.
- Casts from labelled double to other labelled types are lossy if there are any tagged_na's.

Does this sound reasonable? Have I missed something?

Other things that came up:
- Some tests assumed that `[[` would return an unclassed result. Should this continue to be the case?
- There's an "old style" `is.labelled` function -- should that be deprecated in favour of a new `is_labelled`, for consistency?
- Should `new_*` and `validate_*` functions be exported?
- I didn't touch the pillar bits. I guess most of that we could get from vctrs now, though?
- Maybe there should be proper C++ constructors? For now I've just slapped `vctrs_vctr` to the back of the class vectors in there.
- Working around the fact that the underlying data type could at any point be any of the three possible caused quite a bit of headache. I wonder if some sort of union type abstraction could help with this? Not sure how exactly that kinf od thing would work, though.

I've yet to do ptype2 and casting for labelled_spss. I had some stabs at it, but couldn't quite work out how to implement them without duplicating too much of the logic from the base class. At the moment all the old tests pass, but behaviour wouldn't be as expected of a full vctrs vector.

title: Column selection and row limiting on read
description:
Implements selective column reading (#248) powered by **tidyselect**.

General strategy is to do two reads: one with 0 rows to find the column names to use with `vars_select()`; and a second read for the full file with just the selected columns. The additional read adds a bit of overhead (which also scales with the number of rows in the data), but performs decently compared to a full read (c.f. [this benchmark](https://github.com/tidyverse/haven/issues/248#issuecomment-471053100)).

To facilitate the first read, an `n_max` argument is also implemented (with ReadStat's `row_limit` API). Currently ReadStat doesn't support limiting to 0 rows (used as "all" instead), so 0-row behaviour is faked at the C++ level by just reading 1 row and not returning it when the user asks for `n_max = 0` at the R level.

title: Add SPSS's display widths to haven
description: This pull request adds the ability for haven to read and write SPSS's display widths. This field controls only how wide the field appears in the SPSS software and does not affect data storage at all. According to the readstat library, this field is irrelevant for SAS and STATA data files. Display widths are written if the appropriate attribute ("display_width") is set for a given column. The default in Readstat is a display width of 8, and so only non-8 values are preserved as attributes when reading a .sav file. This minimizes the impact on those who are not using display widths. Commit acd4e2d adjusts the .sav file used for testing to have the default display widths, so that they are ignored.

title: fix #245 by making sure string columns always have a max_length >= 1
description:
In https://github.com/WizardMac/ReadStat/commit/39793f9b0dcda35b47fb4796e4553e618c93125d which was integrated into haven at https://github.com/tidyverse/haven/commit/891bccaf314e725d1eac96475b6c5e363ff23479 new code was created to handle the writing of very large strings. However, in so doing, the line that automatically set string columns with width 0 to have a width of 255 was removed. When ReadStat tries to write a string column with width 0, this creates an infinite loop condition on this line https://github.com/WizardMac/ReadStat/blob/master/src/spss/readstat_sav_write.c#L210 since extra_fields starts at -1 and keeps decrementing, and therefore will never be 0, stopping the loop. One fix to this is in the present pull request, which simply makes the minimum length of a string column in haven 1, rather than 0. 

Another fix would be to ReadStat itself, at https://github.com/WizardMac/ReadStat/blob/master/src/spss/readstat_sav_write.c#L903 , to reintroduce the code that overrides a 0 width to 255 as it used to do here https://github.com/WizardMac/ReadStat/blob/085e04876b190a5b7f1d6ad6824c0fa8e74689b6/src/spss/readstat_sav_write.c#L748

I'm unsure which approach is the best, but fixing this issue in haven can't hurt.

title: Fix for #172 (labels) and #177 (variable label).
description:
This is a fix for:
#### #172

`as_factor.labelled` should always keep predefined labels, even if they have no observations in the data (implicit missing). As discussed, the resulting levels should be sorted by values if `x` is a numeric vector, this satisfies your example:

``` R
likert <- labelled(sample(5, 100, replace = TRUE), c("Very Good" = 1, "Very Bad" = 5))
as_factor(likert)
# > ...
# > Levels: Very Good 2 3 4 Very Bad
```

And mine (current version of `as_factor` would sort levels alphabetically):

``` R
labs <- c("Agree", "Neutral", "Disagree")
semant <- labelled(c("Neutral", "Agree", "Don't know"), setNames(labs, labs))
as_factor(semant)
#> ...
#> Levels: Agree Neutral Disagree Don't know
```
#### #177

as_factor should preserve the variable label. I'm thinking this should be done for **all** `as_factor` methods, and not just for `labelled` (since any type of vector can have a label).

title: Fix missings handling
description:
This is a WIP that currently implements the R side.

I first set out to remove the `is_na` mechanism and replace it with the `missings` attribute we talked about. However I think it will make the analysis less comfortable if we drop the information about which labels correspond to missing values because this is useful to understand a dataset. So this preserves both attributes.
- The user can supply either `is_na`, `missings`, or both. When `is_na` is supplied, we work out the `missings` attribute automatically.
- In the case some pseudo-missing values don't have labels attached, both `is_na` and `missings` will need to be supplied. It's up to the user to make sure that the missingness pattern implied by `missings` is consistent with the one implied by `is_na`. In other words, the `missings` pattern should always be identical or broader than the implied `is_na` pattern. An error is issued when they are not consistent.
